chunks: From him, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt; is it upon him to perform Hajj? He said: Yes. Indeed, the Hajj of Islam is obligatory upon every Muslim who is able to walk. And indeed, most of those who performed Hajj with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did so on foot. And indeed, he (peace be upon him and his family) passed by Kura' al-Ghaim, and they complained to him of exhaustion and hardship, so he said: 'Tighten your girdles and walk slowly,' so they did that and it went away from them. So do not see a contradiction between these two reports and the earlier reports, because the explanation for them is one of two things: One is that they are to be understood as referring to recommendation (istihbab), because whoever is able to walk is recommended to perform Hajj, and if it is not obligatory, he incurs punishment for leaving it, and the utterance of the name of obligation upon it is a form of concession. And we have already explained that what is strongly recommended is permissible to be called obligatory even if it is not a duty. And the second explanation is that they are to be understood as a form of precautionary piety (taqiyyah), because that is the view of some of the Sunnis, and that which indicates that the Hajj of the debtor (mu'sir) does not suffice for him if he becomes wealthy is the Hajj of Islam.

key_terms.الْمُعْسِرِ: The debtor / one with a debt

ai.seo_question: Is a person with a debt obligated to perform Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a debtor remains obligated to perform Hajj if capable of walking, emphasizing the primacy of the Hajj of Islam over debt settlement. The text reconciles apparent contradictions regarding the Prophet’s companions by interpreting their mode of travel through the lenses of strong recommendation (istihbab) or taqiyyah, while clarifying that the Hajj of the debtor (hajj al-mu'sir) is distinct from the obligatory Hajj of Islam.
